messages:
incident-bot: Pager: increased 5xx and sustained high p99 for serve-text in eu-central-1, affected model group rwd/psi-* starting ~03:15 UTC. Assigned to on-call @Alex.

Alex: Acknowledged. Triage starting. Quick signal: p99 up from 220ms -> 1.5s, error rate ~12%. Checking recent deploys and model flips.

Mei (runtime): I see a config change: we rolled a key-version bump (kv_v2) for rwd/psi-medium at 03:02 UTC to support metadata tags. Canary passed basic tests but no load spike.

Carlos (sre): Nodes show elevated disk IO on KV shard 7 and heavy write amplification. Also noticed more GC pauses in the cache tier. No GPU OOMs.

Nikhil (batching): Batching service started splitting requests across new key namespaces when it saw the kv_v2 header; we inadvertently disabled request coalescing for those requests which increases write-per-request. Looks like ~3x more KV mutations.

Alex: That matches: new key namespace + lost coalescing -> write storm -> cache eviction -> increased backend fetch -> higher latency and 5xxs. Mitigation options: 1) Re-enable coalescing for kv_v2 quickly; 2) Roll back key-version feature; 3) Rate-limit rwd/psi-* in eu-central-1. Which is safest fast path?

Mei: Re-enabling coalescing is a runtime flag flip, low-risk. I'll push the toggle to eu-central-1 now. Command: 
```
redwood runtime feature-toggle set --region eu-central-1 --service batching --feature coalescing=true --dry-run=false
```

Ops-Bot: Feature toggle executed by Mei at 03:28 UTC. Propagating to 6/6 nodes.

Carlos: After toggle, observed KV mutations per-second drop ~65% and disk IO falling. Error rate dropping to 4% within 5 mins. p99 still elevated but trending down.

Alex: Good. I'll also temporarily throttle new canary traffic for rwd/psi-medium until we validate kv_v2 key schema tests. Command to throttle: 
```
redwood traffic-control update --model rwd/psi-medium --region eu-central-1 --canary-rate 0
```

Nikhil: Throttle applied at 03:36 UTC. Canary traffic now 0.

Priya: Customer ops: two customers (acct 4456, acct 9988) reported truncation and 502 errors. They've been notified of mitigation and we opened ticket RDW-5009 for the escalations.

Mei: I'll run the regression-suite that verifies coalescing behavior across key versions. I spotted a code-path in batching where header parsing returns 'unknown' for partial metadata and we were treating it as 'no-coalesce'. Fix patch ready, applying to staging then prod.

Alex: Timeline so far: start 03:15 UTC, mitigation toggle at 03:28, throttle at 03:36, error rate baseline at ~03:50. We'll keep tracking.

Ops-Bot: Alert: p99 latency back within 20% of baseline at 03:51 UTC; 5xxs ~0.8% at 03:55 UTC.

Alex: Ok, next steps: create post-incident artifacts and owners. I'm creating the initial action list here so we can file tickets.

Mei: Proposed remediation items:
- RDW-5001: Fix batching header parser to correctly map kv_v2 values -> ensure coalescing preserved. Include unit + integration tests. Owner: Mei. ETA: 48h.
- RDW-5002: Add regression test in canary pipeline that runs mixed key-version traffic and asserts no increase in KV mutations per request. Owner: Mei + Nikhil. ETA: 72h.

Nikhil: Infra/batching items:
- RDW-5003: Add a fallback heuristic to the coalescer to detect high write amplification and auto-enable coalescing for variants that appear to be identical. Owner: Nikhil. ETA: 1 week.
- RDW-5004: Improve batching observability: emit coalescing-ratio metric and per-namespace mutation-per-request metric. Owner: Nikhil/Carlos. ETA: 5 days.

Carlos: SRE items:
- RDW-5005: Add KV shard auto-throttle when write amplification exceeds threshold to prevent cache eviction cascades. Owner: Carlos. ETA: 1 week.
- RDW-5006: Run post-incident capacity review for eu-central-1 cache tier and add capacity plan. Owner: Carlos. ETA: 3 business days.

Priya: Customer/comm items:
- RDW-5007: Prepare incident-communication summary and send to affected customers, include ETA and mitigation steps. Owner: Priya/Customer Ops. ETA: 24h.

Alex: I'll schedule the postmortem meeting and own the RCA doc. Proposed meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Please confirm. Agenda: timeline, root cause, code diff review, test gaps, verification plan, and closure criteria.

Mei: Works for me.

Nikhil: Works. I'll bring a plan for RDW-5003 and RDW-5004.

Carlos: Works. I'll attach relevant Grafana panels and kv shard logs to the ticket.

Priya: Works and will prepare customer comms draft.

Alex: Assigning immediate verification task: Mei, after RDW-5001 lands, run the production-smoke that simulates heavy mixed-version traffic in a canary pool. We'll keep canary disabled until verified.

Mei: Will do. I'll also add a small repro tool snippet to the postmortem: 
```
# repro mixed key-version behavior
python infra/tools/mix_kv_versions.py --model rwd/psi-medium --versions v1,v2 --rate 200 --duration 120
```

Alex: Handoff to overnight on-call (Ops: Carlos) at 04:30 UTC. System stable; toggles applied; canary paused. Action items RDW-5001..RDW-5007 created and owners assigned.

Ops-Bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 03:55 UTC. Severity: Sev3.

Carlos: I'll monitor overnight and escalate if mutation-per-request rises above baseline by 50% or if p99 crosses 1s.

Priya: Sending customer update now to affected accounts with note that we're doing a full postmortem and will share timeline.

Alex: Thanks team. I'll post the RCA doc link in Jira and link back to this thread.
